definition.text: This card's own subtitle -- "find patterns, failures · Opportunities" -- names the loop's diagnostic stage: production failures are mined, clustered and classified into named opportunities before any fix is attempted, feeding 7.2 Experiment rather than a raw bug list. Industry practice states the same shape directly, with classification as a precondition to correction: "Every incident should first be classified before it is corrected." This repo's own target architecture independently commits to a matching discipline for its own review sections, not specifically for mining live agent traces: "at the end of each section a ceremony re-reviews the output, improves the skills that produced it, and the loop continues" -- this is this repo's own stated intent (T-t4-04), not evidence that any platform mines production failures this way. Nothing has been built for this card; status is planned.

evidence.quote: at the end of each section a ceremony re-reviews the output, improves the skills that produced it, and the loop continues.
Every incident should first be classified before it is corrected.

standards.role: Standardizes the raw span/event signals an Analyze stage would mine as its input -- e.g. error.type and gen_ai.response.finish_reasons, defined as an "array of reasons the model stopped generating tokens, corresponding to each generation received."
standards.covers: Does not standardize failure-pattern analysis, clustering, taxonomy, or a "finding"/"opportunity" object -- the standard's own repository status is still Development, and it stops at signal capture.

evidence.text: The closest published, vendor-neutral standard to this card's subject only governs the inputs the card would consume, not the analysis itself: the finish-reasons attribute is defined as an "array of reasons the model stopped generating tokens, corresponding to each generation received," with nothing in the same standard describing a cluster, a classified failure mode, or a finding.

evidence.quote: Array of reasons the model stopped generating tokens, corresponding to each generation received.

tools.name: Error Feed (Future AGI)
tools.note: A named production system implementing this card close to end to end: failing traces are embedded and soft-clustered, then a judge agent classifies each cluster against a fixed taxonomy and emits one concrete next fix.

evidence.text: Failing traces are routed with their span embeddings and grouped by soft clustering into named issues: "HDBSCAN soft-clustering groups them into named issues at prob >= 0.4." A judge agent then runs per cluster and "emits the 5-category 30-subtype classification, the 4-dim trace score, and a single immediate_fix string naming the change to ship today."

evidence.quote: HDBSCAN soft-clustering groups them into named issues at prob >= 0.4.

tools.name: Latitude (Signals)
tools.note: Turns recurring failures into named, tracked problems with a lifecycle (first observation to verified resolution), fed by human annotations and automated flaggers, then auto-generates regression evals from those tracked problems.

evidence.text: "Signals turn recurring failures into named, tracked problems" with example traces, affected-user counts and a lifecycle, fed by human annotations, automated flaggers and scores, with regression evals auto-generated from them.

evidence.quote: Signals turn recurring failures into named, tracked problems

tools.name: MAST (Multi-Agent System Failure Taxonomy)
tools.note: The field's most-cited general-purpose failure taxonomy -- 14 modes in 3 categories, built from 150 expert-annotated traces at kappa=0.88 -- but it is a research artifact, not software, and named production tools (e.g. Error Feed's own 5-category/30-subtype scheme) do not adopt its vocabulary by name.

evidence.text: "This process identifies 14 unique modes, clustered into 3 categories: (i) system design issues, (ii) inter-agent misalignment, and (iii) task verification," built through analysis of 150 expert-annotated traces at kappa = 0.88 inter-annotator agreement.

evidence.quote: This process identifies 14 unique modes, clustered into 3 categories: (i) system design issues, (ii) inter-agent misalignment, and (iii) task verification.

landscape.text: Two different things are both called "analysis" here, and neither is settled across the field. Academic work converges on one general-purpose taxonomy (MAST: 14 modes / 3 categories, kappa=0.88), yet named production systems do not adopt it by name -- Future AGI's own product uses a distinct 5-category/30-subtype scheme, so even mature tools disagree on the output vocabulary this card's "Opportunities" would need. Separately, the mining pipeline itself is converging on one practitioner pattern: "Error analysis is the workflow of pulling failed traces, clustering them by failure mode, labeling root causes, and prioritizing fixes by frequency × business impact" -- embedding failed traces and clustering with HDBSCAN or KMeans (K=5-15 typical), then human- or judge-agent-assigned taxonomy labels, then prioritizing by impact rather than raw frequency. A wider field survey (55 papers, early 2025-April 2026) confirms this is an active, still-fragmenting research area organized along five separate dimensions (taxonomy, attribution, enhancement, monitoring tools, datasets) rather than one settled method or output schema.

evidence.quote: This process identifies 14 unique modes, clustered into 3 categories: (i) system design issues, (ii) inter-agent misalignment, and (iii) task verification.
We collect 55 papers published between early 2025 and April 2026, spanning software engineering, artificial intelligence, and human-computer interaction.
Error analysis is the workflow of pulling failed traces, clustering them by failure mode, labeling root causes, and prioritizing fixes by frequency × business impact.

usage.text: No call shape has been designed for this repo -- this paragraph describes industry precedent, not anything built here. The nearest analogue: a batch of failing traces goes in; clustered, named findings come out. One named production pipeline states its own output fields directly: "A judge agent runs on each cluster, emits the 5-category 30-subtype classification, the 4-dim trace score, and a single immediate_fix string naming the change to ship today." The generic version of the same shape is: pull failed traces, cluster by failure mode, label root causes, prioritize by frequency times business impact, then hand the top clusters to 7.2 Experiment as opportunities.

gaps.what: The only standard touching this card, OpenTelemetry's GenAI semantic conventions, standardizes raw signal capture (error.type, finish_reasons) and nothing about failure clustering, taxonomy, or a "finding" object -- and this repo's own telemetry card (cap-telemetry) already depends on the same standard for the layer this card would sit above.
gaps.why_it_matters: A caller building this card has no interoperable schema to target for its output: every named production system (Error Feed, Latitude) defines its own private classification vocabulary, so an "opportunity" produced here could not be exchanged with another platform even in principle.
gaps.research_query: kb_index.py search "finding schema clustering taxonomy standard agent failure"

gaps.what: 9 of this card's 10 research records carry an explicit correction note dated 2026-09-09 -- an initial fetch had introduced invented statistics, fabricated punctuation, or a claim the re-fetched page did not actually support, and the record was corrected rather than re-asserted. The surviving text is what is cited in this profile.
gaps.why_it_matters: This is the exact failure category this card is about (confidently presented, unreliable output) occurring in the evidence-gathering process itself; it argues for the same scrutiny before any further record is added to this lens uncritically, not just for the platform this card describes.

gaps.what: Production systems found here do not converge on one output vocabulary for "opportunities": MAST's academic 14-mode/3-category taxonomy, Error Feed's 5-category/30-subtype scheme, and Latitude's open-ended named-Signal lifecycle are three different shapes for the same stage's output.
gaps.why_it_matters: If this platform eventually builds this card, picking any one vendor's taxonomy is a design choice this repo has not yet made and the evidence gathered here does not resolve in either direction.
gaps.research_query: kb_index.py search "failure taxonomy convergence standard vocabulary agent"
